name: Hattush
overview: Hattush was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified as the son of Shecaniah. He is noted in Scripture as one who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra during the post-exilic restoration. His lineage and participation in the return highlight his role among the faithful remnant returning from captivity.
namesAndTitles: The name Hattush appears as a proper name in Scripture without an explicit meaning provided. There is no indication that the name was given directly by God, and the biblical record simply identifies him by this name.
familyAndRelationships: Hattush is recorded as the son of Shecaniah, establishing his family connection within the tribe of Judah. Beyond this paternal link, Scripture does not provide additional family relationships for Hattush.
scriptureSignificance: Hattush's significance lies in his inclusion among those who returned with Ezra, marking him as part of the faithful community seeking to restore worship and obedience to God in Jerusalem. His genealogy ties him to the tribe of Judah, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant people during the restoration period. Though not extensively detailed, his mention affirms the collective effort to rebuild and renew God's people after exile.
